rationale: Latency is the primary objective, and Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite already sits at 585ms best / 682ms baseline. No lever left on Gemini (temperature, token cap) can plausibly beat the 50ms epsilon or the +0.03 quality epsilon, given run-to-run latency noise of about 100ms. In rounds 2-4 every other evaluated model failed: gpt-5-4-mini scored speak_and_act=0 (27 speech-only and 20 tool-call-only failures), so gpt-5-4-nano, from the same family, is expected to fail the same way; qwen3-next was too slow (1192ms); deepseek scored well (0.538, 6 premature transfers) but was reverted at 674ms. Llama-4-Maverick is the strongest model not yet run: a mixture-of-experts model with about 17B parameters active per token, competent tool calling, and a fair chance of a faster time-to-first-token than Flash-Lite on serving endpoints. Predicted: latency_ms_median 450-600ms, quality 0.45-0.53, premature_transfers 6-12. Main risks: (1) it may answer with speech only or a tool call only, as the GPT models did, which would lower speak_and_act; (2) it may make more premature transfers than the epsilon-0 gate allows. Caveat: the probe rejected max_completion_tokens for this model (reasoning=none) and accepted max_tokens. If every row errors with 'unknown field max_completion_tokens', the harness needs token_param=max_tokens for this model. That is a configuration fault, not a model failure.
